NKE.rationale: Nike's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating across nearly every dimension. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with net income falling 34.5% YoY. Revenue was essentially flat at $11.28B but down 3% currency-neutral. Gross margin contracted 130bps to 40.2% due to 300bps of tariff headwinds in North America. Operating income collapsed to $650M from $844M a year ago. Cash generation is severely impaired: operating cash flow of $430M in Q3 vs $1.79B in the year-ago quarter, a 76% decline. The balance sheet shows total liabilities of $22.97B against $14.09B equity. Converse revenue plunged 35%. Greater China revenues fell 10% (guided to fall ~20% in Q4). The company recorded a $230M severance charge. Management guided Q4 revenue down 2-4% and deferred full-year guidance to a fall 2026 Investor Day, signaling lack of confidence in near-term visibility. Valuation remains elevated: P/E of 29.2x on depressed earnings, well above the 18.6x low seen in May 2025 when earnings were stronger. P/B of 4.7x is near the bottom of its 4.5-8.4 range but reflects a much weaker ROE (16% vs 32% a year ago). The stock has fallen 29% in the last quarter alone, yet the P/E has expanded from 18.6x to 29.2x as earnings collapsed faster than the price. News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.202 over 90 days, with persistent -1.0 readings in April). Tariff headwinds are expected to persist through Q1 FY27, and rising oil prices (WTI at $108.64, up 76% over the period) threaten further input cost inflation. The 'Win Now' turnaround is proving slower than expected, with management acknowledging external headwinds from Middle East instability, tariffs, and macro volatility. No credible near-term fundamental catalyst exists to re-rate the stock; the next potential catalyst is a fall 2026 Investor Day, which is months away. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating fundamentals, still-elevated valuation on depressed earnings, and no near-term re-rating catalyst.
